Lula is reportedly holding a narrow lead over Flávio Bolsonaro with 75% of Brazil’s votes counted.

It’s now 51% Lula and 48.9% Bolsonaro with nearly 75% of votes counted. Lula seems to be closing in on victory and the mood in his camp is increasingly excited. This would be an absolutely sensational comeback from one of the biggest figures in the modern history of Latin American politics.
Lula has edged further ahead in the latest figures, reportedly taking 50.92% to Bolsonaro’s 49.08% with 69.92% of ballots counted.

The celebratory mood that swept Flávio Bolsonaro’s headquarters moments ago when he overtook Lula in the vote count has disappeared since the president began closing the gap and moved back into the lead. Despite the earlier celebrations, the atmosphere has in some ways been tense since the start of the evening.…

There were screams of joy in Lula’s hotel as he took the lead a few minutes ago. With nearly half of votes counted he now has 50.15% to Bolsonaro’s 49.85%. “It’s going to work out! It’s going to work out! It has to!” one official told me. The mood here is increasingly upbeat with Bolsonaro’s path to victory looking…

Lula’s main bet in trying to overturn Bolsonaro’s lead was to increase turnout, after abstention reached a record high in the first round – which, according to many polls, disproportionately affected the leftist’s voters, who generally live farther from polling stations. The figures are not yet final, but with 24.4%…

Meanwhile, hundreds of Lula supporters have camped out on Paulista Avenue to watch the vote count, which started at 7pm local time. Among them is Camilo Buarque, 35, who came with a bright red banner reading: “Lula: My President”. “I feel so very happy being here and being here fighting for Lula,” Buarque says,…

Flávio Bolsonaro is following the count from the mansion of one of his campaign coordinators in a wealthy area of the capital, Brasília. The dozens of journalists present are being kept separate from Bolsonaro and allied politicians, but from time to time they can hear bursts of celebration – like after a goal –…
And just like that, the race is already tightening further. Bolsonaro now has 50.01% of the vote, while Lula has 49.99% of the vote with just over 13.5% of ballots counted.
With 5% of votes counted Lula has taken an early lead with 51% of votes to Bolsonaro’s 48.87%. This is going to be a tight race and a very long night.

One of the most popular figures in Flávio Bolsonaro’s party, congressman Nikolas Ferreira, indicated that the far right could use the extension of voting hours as grounds to challenge the election result in the event of a victory by Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Speaking to journalists outside the mansion in Brasília…
